name: Rajma Chawal
cuisine: Punjabi / North Indian (also Jammu and Himachal)

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ tsp (level) for the rajma, split, plus a pinch for the rice

ingredients.name: Oil (sunflower, groundnut or mustard) or ghee
Tomato
ingredients.householdMeasure: 1 medium tomato, grated or finely chopped

equipment: A bowl for soaking the rajma and a small bowl for soaking the rice
Kadai or a heavy pan (about 20 cm) for the masala
Small heavy saucepan (about 14–16 cm) with a tight lid for the rice
Fine strainer or sieve for rinsing rice
Wooden spoon or flat spatula, a ladle, and a fork for fluffing rice
Measuring spoons and a ¼ cup measure

steps.title: The night before, measure ¼ cup (50 g) dried rajma into a bowl
steps.text: The night before, measure ¼ cup (50 g) dried rajma into a bowl
steps.visualCue: a small heap of dark-red beans
steps.cameraCheck: the rajma in the bowl
steps.videoShot: rajma pouring from the measuring cup into the bowl

steps.title: Rinse the rajma 2–3 times in water and drain
steps.text: Rinse the rajma 2–3 times in water and drain
steps.tip: pick out any small stones, shrivelled or broken beans.
steps.visualCue: the water runs clear, with no dust or grit
steps.cameraCheck: the rinsed rajma
steps.videoShot: a hand swirling beans in water

steps.title: Cover the rajma with 250 ml (1 cup) water and leave it to soak for 8–10 hours (overnight)
steps.text: Cover the rajma with 250 ml (1 cup) water and leave it to soak for 8–10 hours (overnight)
steps.tip: in hot Mumbai weather, soak in the fridge if it will be more than 10 hours, so the water does not ferment.
steps.visualCue: next morning the beans are about double in size, plump, with smooth (not wrinkled) skins
steps.cameraCheck: the soaked rajma next to the bowl's water line
steps.videoShot: before/after of the bowl, small dry beans versus swollen beans

steps.title: Drain and throw away the soaking water, rinse the beans once, and put them into the pressure cooker with 300 ml fresh water
steps.text: Drain and throw away the soaking water, rinse the beans once, and put them into the pressure cooker with 300 ml fresh water
steps.tip: do not cook in the soaking water. Discarding it removes some of the compounds that cause gas.
steps.visualCue: water about 3 cm above the beans
steps.cameraCheck: the open cooker with rajma and water
steps.videoShot: fresh water poured over the beans in the cooker

steps.title: Add ¼ tsp of the salt, stir, and close the lid
steps.text: Add ¼ tsp of the salt, stir, and close the lid
steps.visualCue: lid locked and the weight (whistle) in place
steps.cameraCheck: the closed cooker
steps.videoShot: salt sprinkled in and the lid locked

steps.title: Pressure cook on medium heat for 6–7 whistles (about 20 min), then turn off the heat and let the pressure drop on its own
steps.text: Pressure cook on medium heat for 6–7 whistles (about 20 min), then turn off the heat and let the pressure drop on its own
steps.tip: older rajma can need 8–10 whistles. Never force the lid open while there is still pressure.
steps.visualCue: whistles counted, then the valve drops and the hissing stops
steps.cameraCheck: the cooker on the flame
steps.videoShot: the cooker whistling

steps.title: Measure ⅓ cup (60 g) rice into a small bowl and rinse it 3 times in water
steps.text: Measure ⅓ cup (60 g) rice into a small bowl and rinse it 3 times in water
steps.visualCue: the water goes from milky to nearly clear
steps.cameraCheck: the rinsed rice in the bowl
steps.videoShot: hand swirling rice in cloudy water

steps.title: Cover the rice with fresh water and leave it to soak
steps.text: Cover the rice with fresh water and leave it to soak
steps.tip: soaking gives longer, fluffier basmati grains. For sona masoori, 10 min is enough.
steps.visualCue: the grains turn opaque white
steps.cameraCheck: the rice soaking in the bowl
steps.videoShot: water poured over the rice

steps.title: Finely chop 1 small onion (60 g)
steps.text: Finely chop 1 small onion (60 g)
steps.visualCue: small, even pieces about the size of a rice grain
steps.cameraCheck: the chopped onion on the board
steps.videoShot: knife chopping the onion

steps.title: Grate or finely chop 1 medium tomato (80 g)
steps.text: Grate or finely chop 1 medium tomato (80 g)

steps.cameraCheck: the tomato pulp in a bowl
steps.videoShot: tomato rubbed on the grater

steps.text: Grate ¾ inch ginger (4 g), finely chop 2–3 garlic cloves (5 g), and slit 1 green chilli
steps.visualCue: a small pile of each, chilli split lengthwise
steps.cameraCheck: the three piles on the board
steps.videoShot: ginger on the grater, then garlic chopped

steps.title: Chop 1 tbsp coriander leaves

steps.title: Open the cooker and check that the rajma is completely soft
steps.text: Open the cooker and check that the rajma is completely soft
steps.tip: if any beans are firm, add 50 ml water and cook 2–3 more whistles. Undercooked kidney beans can cause stomach upset and never soften later in the masala. Keep all the cooking liquid; it goes into the curry.
steps.visualCue: a bean squashes into a smooth paste between thumb and finger, with no hard or chalky centre; the cooking liquid is reddish-brown
steps.cameraCheck: one bean pressed flat between two fingers
steps.videoShot: the open cooker, then a fingertip squashing a bean

steps.title: Heat 2 tsp (10 g) oil or ghee in a kadai on medium heat
steps.text: Heat 2 tsp (10 g) oil or ghee in a kadai on medium heat
steps.visualCue: the oil shimmers and flows easily
steps.cameraCheck: hot oil in the kadai
steps.videoShot: oil swirled around the pan

steps.title: Add ½ tsp cumin seeds and 1 bay leaf, and let them crackle
steps.text: Add ½ tsp cumin seeds and 1 bay leaf, and let them crackle

steps.cameraCheck: cumin and bay leaf in the oil
steps.videoShot: close-up of cumin bubbling

steps.title: Add the chopped onion and sauté until light golden brown
steps.text: Add the chopped onion and sauté until light golden brown
steps.tip: if it starts sticking, add 1 tbsp of the rajma liquid and keep stirring.
steps.visualCue: evenly golden, soft, sweet-smelling onion
steps.cameraCheck: the golden onion

steps.title: Add the ginger, garlic and green chilli, and sauté

steps.cameraCheck: the pan with aromatics mixed in
steps.videoShot: aromatics tossed into the onion

steps.title: Lower the heat and add ⅛ tsp turmeric, ½ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder and 1 tsp coriander powder, then stir for 20 seconds
steps.text: Lower the heat and add ⅛ tsp turmeric, ½ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder and 1 tsp coriander powder, then stir for 20 seconds
steps.tip: if the pan looks dry, splash in 1 tbsp of rajma liquid so the spices don't burn.

steps.text: Pour in all the rajma cooking liquid (about 150–200 ml; top up with water to reach 200 ml) and stir

steps.title: Add the remaining salt (about ¼ tsp, to taste) and bring to a boil

steps.cameraCheck: the bubbling rajma

steps.title: Mash 8–10 beans against the side of the kadai with the back of the ladle
steps.text: Mash 8–10 beans against the side of the kadai with the back of the ladle

steps.title: Lower the heat, partly cover, and simmer, stirring every 3 minutes. Start the rice (steps 25–29) now
steps.text: Lower the heat, partly cover, and simmer, stirring every 3 minutes. Start the rice (steps 25–29) now
steps.tip: rajma thickens more as it stands, so stop while it is slightly looser than you want.
steps.visualCue: the gravy thickens and turns velvety, but still flows off the spoon
steps.cameraCheck: a spoonful of gravy lifted from the pan
steps.videoShot: thick gravy dripping slowly from the ladle

steps.title: Drain the soaked rice in the strainer
steps.text: Drain the soaked rice in the strainer
steps.visualCue: rice is drained, with no pool of water
steps.cameraCheck: the drained rice in the strainer
steps.videoShot: water draining out of the sieve

steps.title: Bring 130 ml water with a pinch of salt to a boil in the small saucepan
steps.text: Bring 130 ml water with a pinch of salt to a boil in the small saucepan
steps.visualCue: a rolling boil
steps.cameraCheck: the boiling water in the pan
steps.videoShot: bubbles rising in the small pan

steps.title: Add the drained rice, stir once gently, and let it come back to a boil
steps.text: Add the drained rice, stir once gently, and let it come back to a boil

steps.title: Cover tightly, turn the heat to the lowest setting, and cook without opening
steps.text: Cover tightly, turn the heat to the lowest setting, and cook without opening
steps.tip: don't lift the lid or stir; the trapped steam does the cooking.
steps.visualCue: when you finally peek, no water is left and small steam holes dot the surface

steps.videoShot: lid placed on the pan, flame turned down

steps.title: Turn off the heat and leave the rice covered to rest
steps.text: Turn off the heat and leave the rice covered to rest
steps.visualCue: grains firm up and separate
steps.cameraCheck: the covered pan off the heat
steps.videoShot: hand switching off the burner

steps.title: Crush ½ tsp garam masala and 1 tsp kasuri methi into the rajma, stir, and simmer 1 more minute
steps.text: Crush ½ tsp garam masala and 1 tsp kasuri methi into the rajma, stir, and simmer 1 more minute
steps.visualCue: green-brown flecks and a warm, fragrant aroma
steps.cameraCheck: the kasuri methi falling into the pan
steps.videoShot: palms rubbing kasuri methi over the rajma

steps.title: Turn off the heat, remove the bay leaf, and stir in most of the coriander leaves
steps.text: Turn off the heat, remove the bay leaf, and stir in most of the coriander leaves

steps.text: Open the rice and fluff it gently with a fork

steps.cameraCheck: a forkful of fluffed rice

reasons: the home plate gives about 18 g plant protein and 12 g fibre with only 2 tsp oil, no frying, no cream and no added sugar; the main drawback is that about 40% of the calories come from white rice, so it is carb-heavy. Restaurant and cloud-kitchen rajma usually uses 1.5–3 tbsp oil, ghee or butter (Goila's is advertised as desi-ghee rajma), sometimes cream, more salt, and a larger rice portion, often with a ghee sachet on top.

researchRating.basis: rajma chawal is one of North India's most loved comfort meals ("Sunday rajma chawal"), with top recipes rated almost perfectly by hundreds of home cooks and Mumbai food guides listing many dedicated spots. It loses a little because the overnight soak makes it a plan-ahead dish, and it is a less common restaurant order in Mumbai than chole or dal.

storage: Rajma curry: fridge-safe for 3 days in an airtight container; it tastes better the next day. Freezer: up to 2–3 months. Boiled, drained plain rajma also freezes well for 3 months, which turns the next batch into a 30-minute dish. Rice: cool it quickly (within 1 hour), refrigerate, and eat within 1 day. Do not leave cooked rice at room temperature for long, especially in Mumbai's heat. Freezing cooked rice in flat portions works for up to 1 month. Reheating: add 2–4 tbsp water to the rajma (it thickens), and heat on the stove until bubbling or microwave 1.5–2 min, stirring halfway. Sprinkle rice with 1 tbsp water, cover, and microwave about 1 min until steaming hot throughout.
leftoverRemix: make rajma-rice tikki wraps. Mash leftover thick rajma with leftover rice, 1 tbsp besan, chopped onion and coriander, shape into 3–4 patties and pan-fry in 1 tsp oil until crisp. Roll them in a wholewheat roti with mint chutney, sliced onion and a dash of chaat masala. Or simmer leftover rajma and rice together with a little water and cheese for a quick rajma "burrito bowl" topped with salsa-style kachumber.
burnOff: Running: about 7.7 km at about 70 kcal per km. Walking: about 10.8 km at a brisk pace (est.), using about 50 kcal per km. Rajma curry alone (about 320 kcal): about 4.6 km running or 6.4 km walking (est.).
